# FLX-3403: the related tables cannot be generated as declared

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

FLUX generates the exposes of one contract together: every key the contract declares is laid out from the row index and never repeats, and every foreign key takes a key its parent's rows hold. A relationship whose target the Simulation does not generate from statistics, a key whose declared range or bins hold fewer values than its rows, a one_to_one child with more rows than its parent, a nullFraction on a key column or on a relationship whose joinType is inner, a key declared with a draw that would repeat values, column types that differ between a foreign key and its target, a key column nothing produces, and two relationships that set one column without one implying the other are refused before any row is drawn. So are the declarations that shape how children are placed: a counts entry whose minChildren the child rows or the shape cannot meet (too few child rows for the eligible parents, or a minimum above the most children the shape allows), whose parentWhen leaves no parent eligible or reads beyond the parent's own row, or that sits on a relationship the layout cannot place (a key, a bridge side, an implied or weighted relationship); a required sum, min or max over the children with no ifNone where a parent can have no children, which would leave it NULL; a link condition on an inner relationship, on a key, or on a relationship another one implies; a bridge whose side is named twice, is one_to_one, carries a nullFraction or has more rows than the pairs of its parents; and a weight on a relationship that cannot pick its parents by one, on a parent column that is not a number, or whose published values are negative or all zero. A reference expose is refused when a cell its profile publishes does not fit its column, as a decimal with more digits than its precision or a number outside the range its type holds. The message names the expose, the column or relationship, and the change to make; a parentWhen that leaves no parent eligible also names the relationship and the condition. A history is refused when its emit has no validity window (one natural entity with a start and an end of one DATE or TIMESTAMP type), when its until, openEnd, chain or start bins leave no room inside timeBounds for the versions an entity takes, when a tracked column is not categorical, names a level it does not declare or has no transition row for a level a chain can reach, or when its parent is not a to-one relationship. An asOf entry is refused when its relationship does not reach the natural entity of an emit that declares a history, its date is not a DATE or TIMESTAMP column, or a rule sets a column the contract requires from a row read as of a date where its entity has no version, which would write NULL. A snapshots, events or periods entry is refused when its of names no emit with a history (or the projected emit itself), when a column it names is missing from the history's emit or has another type, when the projected emit declares rows of its own, when an events type has no text for a reason its events carry, when a before or after column maps a column the contract requires that the kept ops would leave NULL, when a when reads a column the version does not hold, or when a periods entry has no grain, no timeBounds, or more periods than a run holds. A DATE or TIMESTAMP column of a history's emit is refused when it declares no range or bins, or a range or bins outside timeBounds, and so is a relationship whose parent is a periodic emit, whose rows grow with the window.
